title: TESS pixels show that 23 of 24 resolved flare-inactive ultra-fast M dwarfs of Ramsay et al. 2022 carry another star's period; with on-target rotators the main-sequence CPV deficit is not significant
abstract: We tested in TESS 2-minute pixels whether the period of an M-dwarf 'ultra-fast rotator' (P < 0.3 d) belongs to the target. For each target pixel file we fitted a 3-harmonic signal at the period in every pixel and compared point-spread-function fits at the target and at every Gaia DR3 neighbour. We processed 1,032 files: 932 rapid rotators of the campaign CPV samples and 39 literature stars. Of the 29 flare-inactive ultra-fast rotators of Ramsay et al. (2022), 24 have a resolved class: 23 have the period off the target, at 8-90 arcsec, and only TIC 85407625, a known RV-variable binary, is on target. Gaia DR3 classes 13 of the 23 signal sources as eclipsing binaries (9), delta Scuti/gamma Doradus pulsators (3) or RS CVn (1). All 7 resolved stars of the Doyle et al. (2022) control sample are on target (Fisher p = 3e-6). Thus the missing flares of these stars need no new physics. Among the 368 main-sequence stars that carry the CPV test, 73% of resolved stars at P = 0.08-0.2 d are off target, against 3.5% in 1-24 Myr members. eRASS1 saturated-corona probabilities are 0.95 for on-target and 0.36 for off-target stars. Our classes agree with a second pixel method for 97.6% and with two centroid methods for 91-92% of resolved stars; X-ray data show that the centroid methods miss some blends. The dips of the main-sequence CPV TIC 35227582 are on its co-moving 9-arcsec companion. With pixel weights, the frozen contraction (x-only) model predicts 3.3 (1.7-5.5) main-sequence CPVs for 1 observed (p = 0.19); with the four-method consensus, 4.4 (2.4-6.7) for 2 (p = 0.23). A rate factor of 0.3-0.5 at fixed x stays possible. Limitations: a two-Gaussian PSF, mostly one sector per star, subsampled young stars and small numbers of genuine old ultrafast stars.

display.caption: Periodic signal images (signal over null error, 11 x 11 TESS pixels) of the 29 flare-inactive ultra-fast rotators of Ramsay et al. 2022 (R22) and the 10 stars of Doyle et al. 2022 (D22). Blue circle: target (Gaia DR3 position at the sector epoch); orange cross: fitted position of the variable source. Red pixels vary in phase with the aperture light curve; blue pixels vary in anti-phase (a bright variable star in the pipeline background estimate). Labels give the period and our class.

(a) eRASS1 probability of a saturated corona (709005b5) for rapid rotators whose TESS period is on target (blue) or off target (orange) in our pixel test, eROSITA-DE sky. (b) Fraction of resolved stars with an off-target period against the TESS period for main-sequence stars in the x range of the CPV test, 1-24 Myr members and 35-750 Myr members; bars are 95% Wilson intervals.

(a) CPVs among main-sequence rapid rotators at the corotation ratio x of young CPV hosts: prediction of the frozen x-only model (blue, 95% bootstrap interval) and observed count (orange) for no correction, X-ray weights (709005b5), our pixel weights and variants, and the four-method consensus. p is the probability of the observed count or fewer. (b) Profile likelihood of the main-sequence rate factor at fixed x; the dotted line marks the 95% level.

citations.reason: We rerun its code to rebuild stellar parameters and per-star eRASS1 saturation probabilities, reuse its rate model, and confirm with TESS pixels its inference that X-ray-quiet main-sequence rapid rotators carry periods of neighbours.

We repeat its main-sequence CPV test with pixel-verified rotators; the deficit becomes non-significant, and one of its two main-sequence CPVs has its dips on the companion. We reuse its S1-S55 periods, labels and efficiencies.
